  "text": "The house came with a telephone mounted inside the pantry.

No dial. No cord.

During the viewing, I asked whether it worked.

“Only for emergencies,” the agent said, and shut the door.

Three weeks after I moved in, it rang.

I was chopping onions. I remember because I answered with the knife still in my hand.

“Don't go upstairs,” a woman whispered.

“Who is this?”

Above me, a floorboard creaked.

I lived alone.

“Put the knife down,” she said. “He'll take it from you.”

I hung up and drove to my sister's.

The police found nothing. No broken windows, no footprints. They couldn't find the telephone either.

When I returned, it was back.

Beside it, someone had drawn a small pencil mark on the wall.

Over the next month, it rang six times.

Don't start the car.

Leave the bathroom now.

Whatever knocks tonight, let it finish.

Each time, I obeyed.

Each time, another mark appeared.

On the seventh call, the woman was crying.

“I'm sorry,” she said. “I thought if I kept you alive long enough, someone would answer mine.”

The pantry door closed behind me.

I pushed against it until my shoulder bruised. Through the wood, I heard someone enter the kitchen and begin chopping.

The receiver was still in my hand.

It had a dial now.

I called my sister. A stranger answered.

I called the police. The same stranger answered.

Then I noticed writing beneath the pencil marks: a telephone number, scratched so deeply the plaster showed.

I dialed.

Beyond the pantry door, the chopping stopped.

My own voice answered.

“Who is this?”"
}
